title: Top-degree cohomology of a total tensor of bounded-above free complexes
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $P^\bullet,Q^\bullet$ be bounded-above cochain complexes of finite free $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], with $P^i=0$ for $i>a$ and $Q^j=0$ for $j>b$. Form the direct-sum total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] with differential $d(p\otimes q)=d_Pp\otimes q+(-1)^{\deg p}p\otimes d_Qq$. Then the canonical map $H^a(P^\bullet)\otimes_R H^b(Q^\bullet)\to H^{a+b}(\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_R Q^\bullet))$ induced by the top-degree tensor representatives is an isomorphism.

source.place: Agent top-degree truncation calculation for direct-sum total tensors of bounded-above free complexes

proof.text: Because $P^i=0$ for $i>a$ and $Q^j=0$ for $j>b$, a summand $P^p\otimes_RQ^q$ can occur in total degree $a+b$ only when $(p,q)=(a,b)$, and all terms in degrees greater than $a+b$ vanish. The outgoing differential from $P^a\otimes_RQ^b$ is therefore zero. In degree $a+b-1$ the only summands that can map to the top term are $(P^{a-1}\otimes_RQ^b)\oplus(P^a\otimes_RQ^{b-1})$, with the total differential prescribed by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

source.place: Direct top-total-degree calculation from the direct-sum tensor convention

proof.text: Since the outgoing differentials $d_P^a$ and $d_Q^b$ have zero target, $H^a(P^\bullet)=P^a/\operatorname{im}(d_P^{a-1})$ and $H^b(Q^\bullet)=Q^b/\operatorname{im}(d_Q^{b-1})$. The image entering the top total term is the sum of the images of $d_P^{a-1}\otimes1$ and $(-1)^a1\otimes d_Q^{b-1}$; the sign does not change that image. Thus the top cohomology is the quotient of $P^a\otimes_RQ^b$ by those two image submodules.

source.place: Direct top-total-degree calculation, identification of the incoming differential

proof.text: Apply tensor right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] first to $\operatorname{im}(d_P^{a-1})\to P^a\to H^a(P^\bullet)\to0$ and then to $\operatorname{im}(d_Q^{b-1})\to Q^b\to H^b(Q^\bullet)\to0$. The first application identifies the quotient by $\operatorname{im}(d_P^{a-1})\otimes_RQ^b$ with $H^a(P^\bullet)\otimes_RQ^b$; the second identifies its further quotient by the image of $P^a\otimes_R\operatorname{im}(d_Q^{b-1})$ with $H^a(P^\bullet)\otimes_RH^b(Q^\bullet)$. Equivalently, the quotient by the sum of the two incoming images is canonically $H^a(P^\bullet)\otimes_RH^b(Q^\bullet)$.

source.place: Top-degree quotient calculation using right exactness of tensor

proof.text: The quotient map sends a pure top-degree tensor $p\otimes q$ to the cohomology class represented by $p\otimes q$ in the total complex. Therefore the canonical map induced by top-degree tensor representatives is exactly the quotient identification from Step 3, and is an isomorphism.

source.place: Identification of the canonical top-degree representative map

proof_origin.place: Direct top-total-degree calculation for the direct-sum tensor convention, using tensor right exactness
